# Unix listener

The `unix` listener configures Boundary to listen on a Unix domain socket. The `address` parameter specifies the socket path instead of a host and port.

```hcl
listener "unix" {
  purpose = "api"
  address = "/var/run/boundary-api.sock"
}
```

The `unix` listener supports the `api`, `cluster`, and `ops` purposes. You cannot use a Unix socket for the `proxy` purpose on a worker. Use a [TCP listener](/boundary/docs/monitor/listeners/tcp) for that purpose.

You can define the `listener` stanza more than once to make Boundary listen on multiple sockets. A controller requires exactly one listener with the `cluster` purpose. Refer to [Configure multiple listeners](/boundary/docs/monitor/listeners/configure-multiple-listeners) for examples.
